analysis:
Every changed file in this batch is a changelog fragment or documentation, so there is no code diff to trace. I found no concrete regression, but several described behaviors change security-relevant surface and need review when the Swift sources are available.

1. changelog.d/glm53-video-input.md:3 adds decoding of consumer-supplied inline video (data:video/mp4 and data:video/quicktime) in the provider. This is a new untrusted-media parser. T-050 (inline video plaintext in provider temp files) and A-001 are directly relevant. The supplied text does not say whether the decode path avoids temp files or how it bounds parser input, so the T-050 protections cannot be confirmed to cover it. Check that the video path reuses the T-050 protections.

2. glm53-native-prerequisites.md:9 says the SSD prefix store defaults on for the pinned GLM identity. It also says video and image rows never reuse cached prefixes. This falls under T-041 and SEC-035. The tier is unchanged in kind, but the GLM TTL, cacheSalt scoping and per-donation gating are not visible here.

3. glm53-native-prerequisites.md:21 describes a DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE that takes a persistent cache key from a file. It claims release builds do not contain this path. That claim needs source verification, since it would bypass the SE-rooted KEK in T-041 if compiled into release. The new /metrics detail field and the log line expose only a typed reason.

4. glm53-native-prerequisites.md:14 adds coordinator-connected GLM serving, the glm5_next_v1 capability and an aggregate agreement check across catalog, receipt and loaded bytes. This relates to A-004, T-012 and T-027. Weight-hash enforcement is not visible here. Line 23 moves weight hashing to F_NOCACHE reads and says the digests are unchanged.

5. local-responses-continuation.md:4 and hardware-support.md:35-42 add an in-memory store of Responses history, with an LRU for continuation history and a separate response-object store that has no matching eviction. Both contain prompt plaintext (A-001) in local direct mode. They are not persisted across restart. The retention and memory bounds are acknowledged only as docs. Direct-mode access control and the memory-bound claim need source verification.

The threat model has no entry for these new surfaces. No source evidence was supplied to establish a regression.
